problems.title: Reward scaling alone does not bound the true soft Q
problems.source_location: Appendix B, p.25; Appendix C.2, pp.26–27, Eqs.2–3.
claim: Appendix C.2 motivates reward normalization as keeping modeled returns within fixed categorical support.
analysis: Consider a self-transition model with continuous state, uniform actions on \([-1,1]\), reward \(1\), \(\gamma=0.99\), \(V_{\max}=10\) and \(\alpha=1/(10\log2)\). Then \(\alpha H=0.1\), the ordinary discounted reward-return bound is \(100\), and the entropy return is \(10\). The printed scale is \(c=1/11\). The soft Bellman equations give \(V=210/11\) and \(Q=2089/110\simeq18.9909>10\). A categorical output remains inside its atoms by construction; the true soft fixed point does not.
result: The stated reward-only normalization does not generally keep the true entropy-regularized Bellman fixed point inside the chosen support. Categorical network outputs remain bounded by their atoms.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Bound the complete scaled reward-plus-entropy return under explicit global reward, entropy and temperature conditions. A sampled historical maximum alone is not such a bound.
problems.impact_rationale: The central normalizer's stated support control does not bound the true soft Bellman target, even in a simple bounded-reward model. The explicit fixed point lies outside the intended support.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Release bootstrap and entropy correction differ
claim: The paper describes critic bootstrap and empirical task-policy entropy in its normalizer.
analysis: The author normalizer bootstraps using mean reward divided by \(1-\gamma\), without a terminal critic input. Its correction is \[-\alpha\,\mathrm{target\_entropy}/[2(1-\gamma)]\], where target_entropy is minus half the action dimension. This is a dimension-derived heuristic, rather than the stated empirical task-policy entropy and terminal-critic recipe.
result: The current release uses a dimension-based heuristic and reward bootstrap, differing from the stated empirical-entropy and critic-bootstrap recipe.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Use the specified terminal critic and measured entropy, or document the actual alternate recipe and its run mapping.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Parallel success counts can exceed task quotas
problems.source_location: Author envs.py: parallel evaluation episode-completion and success accumulation loop.
claim: The evaluator reports per-task success rates over requested episode counts.
analysis: While awaiting slower parallel environments, the evaluator continues adding successes for a task whose episode quota is already complete. It can therefore produce reported rates \([2,1]\). A success probability cannot exceed one: numerator and denominator are drawn from different episode sets. The frequency and paper-table impact require original episode-duration logs.
result: The current evaluator can count successes outside the episode set in its denominator. The frequency and published-score impact remain unknown.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Stop accumulating every metric for a task after its evaluation quota, or divide by the exact number accumulated.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Checkpoint restoration uses the actor loader for other objects
problems.source_location: Author jaxrl/agent/brc_learner.py, lines 239-243; jaxrl/utils.py, lines 84-90; repository issue 2, Error in brc_learner.load.
claim: The release is expected to restore actor, critic, target critic and temperature states by role.
analysis: All four restore assignments invoke self.actor.load, whose serialization template and retained identity are those of the actor. Changing only filenames does not make actor, critic and temperature model structures interchangeable. The concern was already reported in repository issue \(2\), Error in brc_learner.load, on 2025-10-10; this is historical reproduction, not a new priority claim.
result: Current restore calls use the actor template for other model roles, retaining the known public restoration defect.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Call each role object’s own loader. Current issue/commit records do not establish author adoption of this correction.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
